aig.title: AI video generator
aig.privacy: Everything happens on your PC: your description and the video created are never sent anywhere. Only downloading the engine and model uses the internet, and only when you ask.
aig.needInstall: To create videos, DedCut must download the engine (30 MB) and the Wan 2.1 model (about 6.6 GB in total). It is free and none of it is in the installer.
aig.licences: Licences: stable-diffusion.cpp (MIT); FastWan 2.2, Wan 2.1, VACE and UMT5-XXL (Apache-2.0). None of it is in the installer: everything is downloaded on demand.
aig.remove: Delete the engine and model (frees 6.6 GB)
aig.removeConfirm: Delete the engine and model from your disk? You can download them again later.
aig.promptPh: E.g.: a red fox running through a snowy forest, cinematic
aig.slow: Note: creation is slow on a PC without a powerful graphics card (from a few minutes to over an hour). You can keep editing meanwhile.
aig.textOnly: For now: text to video only (“image to video” needs a much heavier model).
aig.done: Video created: it is in the library and on the timeline.
aig.needPrompt: First write what you want to see in the video.
aig.onlyApp: The generator is only available in the installed DedCut app.
aig.busy: A creation or download is already in progress.
aig.label: AI-generated content
aig.imgHint: With FastWan, your image becomes the first frame of the video and the AI makes it move following your description (e.g. “the strawberry dances and smiles”). With VACE, the AI only keeps the character’s look.
aig.imgNeedModel: To animate an image, DedCut must download a second model (Wan 2.1 VACE 1.3B, 4.3 GB, Apache-2.0).
aig.needImage: First choose the image to animate.
aig.imgSlow: Image mode is about 3 times slower than text mode: expect around ten minutes for 1 second in draft quality.
aig.mVace: Wan 2.1 VACE — keeps a reference character
aig.mFastHint: The best choice: only 3 steps, 24 frames/s, and true image animation (your image becomes the first frame of the video). Up to 15 s in several parts. Apache-2.0 licence.
aig.mWanHint: Older model, smaller but slower and less good-looking. Text only, 5 s maximum.
aig.mVaceHint: Keeps the look of a character from an image, without copying it exactly. Slow on a small graphics card. 5 s maximum.
aig.removeModelConfirm: Delete this model from your disk? You can download it again later.
aig.longHint: Beyond 5 s, the video is created in several 5 s parts that follow each other: each one starts from the last frame of the previous one. Small seams may be visible.
aig.head: AI video
aig.installInfo: Only once: {size} to download. After that everything runs on your PC, without internet.
aig.promptPh2: Describe what happens… e.g. a cute strawberry dances in a kitchen
aig.footer: AI-generated content. The video goes to the library and the timeline.
aig.imgUnsupported: This model cannot animate an image: choose FastWan in the advanced settings.
aig.installVerify: The files are already on your PC: they just need to be checked (a few seconds).
aig.tipEnglish: Tip: be precise — name the character, the action and the place.

ai.title: AI connector
ai.intro: Let an AI like Claude Desktop do the editing: tell it what you want (“cut the silences, add an intro and a progress bar”) and it drives DedCut.
ai.privacy: Between Claude Desktop and DedCut everything stays on your PC (local connection protected by a secret code). The AI only gets the text description of the project (file names, durations, texts), never your videos. Every action is shown and can be undone with Ctrl+Z. Claude Desktop uses your Anthropic account.

ai.off: Connector off: no AI can touch DedCut.
ai.step2: 2. Click “Add to Claude Desktop”, then close and reopen Claude Desktop (get it from claude.ai/download).

d.claude: Very good at editing. Paid: you need an Anthropic API key with credit (this is not the Claude.ai subscription).
d.openai: Paid: you need an OpenAI API key with credit (this is not the ChatGPT Plus subscription).
d.ollama: Free and offline. Install Ollama, then a model that can use tools (example: ollama pull qwen3). Slower and less skilled than an online AI.
d.custom: For LM Studio, another local server or an online service compatible with the OpenAI API. The model must be able to use tools.
d.gemini: Free with a daily request limit: create your key with your Google account. With the free tier, Google may use what you send to improve its services.
d.dedcut: DedCut’s own AI: built in, free and offline. It understands common editing requests (cut silences, subtitles, sound visualizer, title, music, transitions, vertical format…) and answers questions about DedCut. For freer requests, choose an online AI or Ollama.

chat.privacy: What you type and the project description (file names, texts, durations) are sent to the chosen service. Your videos, pictures and sounds are never sent.

upd.title: Updates
upd.installing: Installing… DedCut will close and open again by itself.
upd.privacy: To check, DedCut only reads the latest version number on github.com. Nothing about you or your projects is sent. Every update is signed: DedCut refuses a file changed by someone else.

dcai.done: Done! If you don’t like it, the “Undo” button puts everything back.
dcai.help: I’m DedCut AI, built in and offline. I can: cut silences, add subtitles, a sound visualizer (bars, wave, circle, curve, VU meter), a title (write it in quotes), music from your library, transitions, fades, a progress bar, a Subscribe button, icons, cinema bars, make the video vertical, and edit automatically. I also answer your questions about DedCut (“how do I cut?”, “where is export?”…). For freer requests, choose an online AI or Ollama in the settings.

dcai.qex2: How do I make my video vertical?

dcai.howru: I’m doing great, thanks! Ready to edit your video. What shall we do?
dcai.who: I’m DedCut AI, the assistant built into DedCut. I work offline, right on your PC: I make editing changes and answer questions about DedCut.

q.unknown: I didn’t find the answer. I mostly know DedCut: cutting, speed, sound, texts, subtitles, effects, green screen, format, export… Try other words. For open questions, choose an online AI or Ollama in **{set}**.

q.sfx: **{tab}** tab → **{sfx}**: ▶ to listen, **+** to add it at the playhead.
q.volume: Click the clip → **{audio}** tab on the right → **{vol}** (the **{mute}** button silences it). For the whole project: click an empty spot in the timeline → **{master}**.

q.rec: At the top, click **{tab}**: an OBS-style studio opens. Add your sources (screen or game, round or square webcam, text, image), place them with the mouse, set the sound in the mixer, then **{start}**. While recording: **Pause** (Ctrl+Shift+P) and **Highlight** (Ctrl+Shift+M); **Ctrl+Shift+R** starts or stops, even in a game. The video lands on the Edit timeline.

q.lag: For big videos, DedCut makes a proxy by itself: a light copy just for the preview (the export keeps the real quality). You can also start it: **{media}** tab, on the video → **{proxy}**. Closing heavy apps helps too.
q.zoom: Click the clip → **{anim}** tab on the right → **{motion}** ({zin}…). For a custom move, use keyframes ({k}).
q.kf: Click the clip, place the playhead and press {k} (or **{btn}** on the right). Move forward, then change a value (position, size, opacity…): DedCut animates between the two.
q.crop: Click the clip → **{base}** tab on the right → **{crop}**.
q.colors: **{tab}** tab on the left for a one-click look. To fine-tune (brightness, contrast, saturation…): click the clip → **{col}** tab on the right.
q.effects: Click a clip, then an effect in the **{tab}** tab (hover over it to preview).
q.slide: First import your photos, then **{media}** tab → **{slide}**: pick the photos, the duration, the transition and the movement.
q.text: **{tab}** tab → **{add}**. Type your text on the right, then pick a style and an animation.
q.import: **{tab}** tab → **{imp}**, or drop your files into DedCut. Then drag them onto the timeline (or click **+**).
q.export: The **{exp}** button at the top right (or {k}). MP4 is recommended; there are also GIF, WebM, PNG image and sound only (WAV, M4A). Videos go to Videos\DedCut\Exports.
q.save: {k} or **{menu}** → **{save}**. DedCut also saves your current edit by itself and keeps **{versions}** on the home screen.
q.delproj: On the home screen (**{menu}** → **{home}**), next to the project: **{del}**. It goes to the Windows Recycle Bin; your videos are not touched.
q.undo: {k} or the arrow at the top left. {k2} to redo.
q.delete: Click the clip and press {k}. {k2} (**{ripple}**) deletes it without leaving a gap.
q.split: Place the playhead where you want to cut, then press {k} (or the scissors above the timeline). Right-click → **{here}** works too. To shorten a clip, just drag its edge.
q.lang: Go to the home screen (**{menu}** → **{home}**), then **{set}** → **{lang}**. It changes right away.
q.keys: The main ones: {list}. To see them all (and change them): **{menu}** → **{kb}**.
q.update: DedCut checks for updates by itself and offers to install them. You have version {v}. To check now: **{menu}** → **{upd}**.
q.free: Yes! DedCut is 100% free: no subscription, no ads, no watermark. If you want to help, there’s the ♥ **{sup}** button.
q.privacy: DedCut works offline: your videos stay on your PC and nothing is sent. The internet is only used for updates, downloading models (subtitles, AI video) and online AIs if you choose one.
q.author: DedCut is made by ByKemi. You have version {v}.
q.support: Thank you! The ♥ **{sup}** button at the top right explains everything. Donations help DedCut stay free.
q.online: Click **{set}** at the top of this window and choose Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini or Ollama (free, on your PC). They understand freer requests.
q.start: {start} I can also give you the guided tour.
q.dur: Your video lasts {dur} ({clips}, size {w} × {h}). To change a clip’s length: drag its edge in the timeline, or change **{durL}** in the **{base}** tab on the right.
q.clean: Click the clip → **{audio}** tab on the right → **{clean}**: it removes hiss, fan noise and background noise, on your PC. Your original file is not changed.
q.live: At the top, click **{tab}**: an OBS-style studio opens. In ⚙ Settings, pick YouTube, Twitch, TikTok, Facebook or Kick and paste your **stream key** (YouTube Studio → Go live; Twitch → Dashboard → Settings → Stream). Get your scenes ready (screen + facecam, "Starting soon", "Be right back"…), then **{go}**. You can record the stream at the same time.

help.title: Getting started with music
help.beat1: File > New project: pick the “Beat” template and a tempo.
help.beat2: Steps tab: click the boxes to place kick, snare and hi-hat.
help.beat3: “Listen” loops the pattern; change the swing or use “Suggest a beat”.
help.beat4: “Place in the song” adds the pattern; repeat to build the sequence.
help.beat5: For a bass: instrument track, “Sub bass” preset, then draw notes with the pencil in the piano roll.
help.beat6: Set the volumes in the Mixer tab.
help.voice1: Plug in your mic and wear headphones (avoids feedback).
help.voice2: Settings > Audio: allow the mic and measure the latency once.
help.voice3: Add an audio track, choose the input (track ⋯ menu) and arm it (round button).
help.voice4: Turn on the metronome and a count-in if you like.
help.voice5: Press Record (R). With the loop on, each pass becomes a take, all kept.
help.voice6: Pick the best part in the Audio clip tab (comping), then add the “Clean voice” chain.
help.voice7: If DedCut closes during recording, the take can be recovered at the next start.
help.export1: Listen to the whole song: the master clip light should stay off.
help.export3: Choose the whole song, the format (lossless WAV 24-bit, or lighter M4A) and the sample rate.
help.export4: Choose “stems” to get one track per file, all aligned to the same start.
help.export5: Start the export: the report shows the length, true peak and loudness.
help.export6: Tick “Send to Editing” to use your music in a video.
help.keys1: Space: play / stop · R: record · L: loop · M: metronome.
help.keys2: Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y: undo / redo · Ctrl+S: save.
help.keys3: Ctrl + wheel: zoom · Shift + wheel: move in time · wheel: scroll tracks.
help.keys4: S: split the clip at the playhead · Ctrl+D: duplicate · Delete: delete.
help.keys5: 1 to 7: switch tab (Piano roll, Steps, Clip, Instrument, Effects, Mixer, Session).
help.keys6: Keyboard button at the top: play notes with the middle row of the keyboard.
help.keys7: All shortcuts can be changed in Edit > Keyboard shortcuts.
help.more: Hover a button to see what it does. Everything you do can be undone with Ctrl+Z.

ext.title: Extensions and plugins
ext.safety: An extension is a small sound process. It runs in the audio thread and only sees samples and its settings: no interface, no network, no files, no secrets, and it can neither change nor hide the “Support DedCut” button. An error or a hang puts it in quarantine. This is not full isolation: only install extensions whose author you know.
ext.confirm: Install “{name}” {ver}? Author: {author} · licence: {licence} · source: {source}. It can only process the sound of the tracks you add it to.
ext.confirmUpd: Update “{name}” from {old} to {ver}? The code changed: check the author ({author}) and the source ({source}).

ext.missing: Missing or disabled extensions (sound passes without them): {list}
ext.stuck: The sound was stuck: extensions quarantined ({list}), audio engine restarted
ext.nativeText: DedCut lists the VST3 and CLAP plugins installed on this PC, but does not load them: their audio would need a native engine the Music space doesn't have, and a native plugin cannot be provably isolated here. No plugin code runs during the scan (only folders and the VST3 info file are read).

ext.sdkIntro: An extension is a JSON file with a small JavaScript code called for each block of 128 samples. Here is the format and a complete example (MIT licence) to copy.

id.title: Ideas and analysis
id.local: No sound or note is sent online. No account, no subscription, no cost. Your creations are not used to train any model. Ideas come from DedCut's musical rules (same seed = same result); they arrive on new tracks, your work is never replaced, and Ctrl+Z undoes.
id.genHint: Ideas follow the project key and scale; change the seed for another suggestion. They are not “exclusive”: someone else with the same seed gets the same result.
id.pickAudio: First pick an audio clip in the arrangement.
id.chordsTip: Detects chords and places them on the chord track (fix by hand if needed)
id.chordsDone: {n} chords suggested on the chord track
id.noChords: No clear chords in this sound
id.transTip: A voice or instrument played one note at a time becomes a MIDI clip on a new track
id.transDone: {n} notes transcribed on a new track (check for wrong notes)
id.noNotes: No clear notes found (try a solo voice)
id.centerTip: Simple method for a stereo sound: the center (often the voice) or the sides. This is not real AI separation: parts of other instruments often remain.
id.cleanTip: Adds at the start of the track: hum removal, noise reduction, declicker (can be bypassed to compare)
id.cleanDone: Cleanup chain added: listen with and without (each effect's button)
id.stemsHint: Separating vocals, drums and bass needs a specialized AI model not included in DedCut for now; the methods above are simple alternatives.
id.voiceDone: Voice added on an audio track
id.voiceHint: Only the generic voices installed in Windows. DedCut does not offer to imitate a real person's voice.
id.voiceApp: Only available in the installed DedCut app.

nt.ph: E.g. “the bass is too loud here”
nt.versionsHint: Keep a state of the song (arrangement variant) to come back to or compare. Versions are saved in the project.
nt.collab: Working together: share the project (File > Archive); comments and versions travel with it. There is no DedCut server: two people cannot edit the same project at the same time.

rt.title: Track routing
rt.hint: Circle: where the track sound goes (one output). Box: an extra send to a bus. DedCut refuses any connection that would loop the sound.
rt.legend: Tip: one reverb on a bus fed by sends costs far less processing than a reverb on each track.

sho.titleAi: Catchy title written by the AI
sho.capHint: Tip: create the subtitles first, they help find the best moments and will be in the Shorts.
sho.listening: DedCut is listening to your video…
sho.tooShort: The video is too short for this length: it needs at least {n} s. Choose a shorter length.
sho.none: No good moment found. Try another length.

sho.titles: The AI is writing the titles…

te.cmd: Edit by text (cut by deleting words)

vf.hint: Vertical has its own scenes, made for phones (TikTok, Shorts, Reels). Your horizontal scenes are kept: you can switch back any time.

vf.busy: Stop the live or the recording first to change the format.

vf.onH: Studio in horizontal 16:9: your scenes are back
vf.toVert: Switch the studio to vertical (TikTok scenes)

pf.gameTip: DedCut steps aside so your game gets the power: a less fluid preview, webcam effects computed less often, and the recording reuses the stream's encoding. Your stream keeps its full quality.
pf.gameOn: Game mode on: DedCut leaves the power to your game
pf.autoBr: Automatic bitrate: lowers the stream quality if your connection slows down, then raises it again
pf.share: Record with the stream's encoding: less load on your PC, same quality as the stream
pf.brDown: Slow connection: DedCut lowers the stream quality ({kbps} kb/s) to avoid drops
pf.brUp: Connection is back: the stream is at full quality again ({kbps} kb/s)

h.netTip: Your connection can't keep up: some frames aren't being sent. Turn on automatic bitrate in Settings, or lower the bitrate.
h.netAuto: Your connection can't keep up: DedCut is lowering the quality by itself. If it keeps happening, stop downloads or switch to 720p.
h.encTip: Your PC can't produce the video fast enough: switch to 720p or 30 fps, or turn on game mode.
h.drawTip: The scene is too heavy to draw: remove the webcam background blur or removal, a video or an effect, or lower the quality.

t.title: PC and connection test
t.intro: DedCut encodes a little video in each quality, measures how long your scene takes to draw, and checks what your connection managed to send during your streams. It takes about ten seconds.
t.netUnknown: not measured yet: do a stream and DedCut will remember
t.why: It leaves headroom for your game.
t.recoNone: Even the lowest quality is tight: close other programs, then run the test again.
t.busy: Stop the stream and recording to change the quality.
